What the Ocean County Clerk does for a seller

Your deed ends up with the Ocean County Clerk, a constitutional officer who oversees the filing and recording of every paper that touches ownership or transfer of real estate in the county. Passports and county elections run through the same office, so expect a busy counter. Few sellers appear at the counter themselves, since an attorney or title company usually files for them, yet the signature on the deed is still yours, which is why knowing the process is worth the few minutes it takes.

For a seller, the moment of recording is when the land record changes hands. The state's transfer fee is collected at that point too. Mail or bring the deed with every required form attached, because a package missing a page or an affidavit can come back unrecorded and push your closing date out.

Clerk office locations and hours

The main office sits in the courthouse at 118 Washington Street in Toms River, and three more service points cover other parts of the county.

Ocean County Clerk locations and hours
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Main office, Courthouse118 Washington Street, Toms River(732) 929-2018Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, counter service until 4
Northern Ocean County225 4th Street, Room 211, Lakewood(732) 370-8850Monday to Friday, 8 to 4:30, counter service until 4
County Connection1201 Hooper Avenue, Toms River (Ocean County Mall, near JCPenney)(732) 288-7777Open daily, regular mall hours
Southern Service Center179 South Main Street, Room 106, Manahawkin(609) 597-1500Mon and Fri 8 am to 4:30 pm; Tue to Thu 8 am to 8 pm; in-person service until 4 pm on Mon and Fri

Manahawkin keeps its doors open until 8 pm midweek, Tuesday through Thursday, a good fit for a seller who cannot get away during the day. Holidays close the courthouse, north and south offices, so phone ahead before driving anywhere with a deed.

What does a deed need before the clerk will record it?

First, it has to go to the clerk for the county where the land actually sits, with the transfer fee paperwork attached. If a deed lands in the wrong county, it is recorded again in the right one. Form RTF-3 gets the State fee refunded, and the county share is claimed back from the office that took it in error.

  • State the full consideration on the deed, since the realty transfer fee is figured on that amount.
  • Any deed that claims an exemption, whether full or partial, needs Form RTF-1, the Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller.
  • New-construction houses need the words NEW CONSTRUCTION across the top of page one, plus an affidavit.
  • A deed over $1,000,000 also carries Form RTF-1EE for the percent fee.

County recording charges are added to the state fee, and the clerk sets that schedule. Phone the office for the current amount before you send anything.

How much transfer fee will an Ocean County seller owe?

The fee works in price brackets, counted per $500. Where the price is $350,000 or lower, the first $150,000 costs $2.00 per $500, the stretch from $150,000 to $200,000 costs $3.35, and anything beyond that costs $3.90. A price above $350,000 uses a separate schedule that opens at $2.90 per $500 and climbs to $4.80 in the band from $200,000 to $550,000.

A typical owned home in the county is valued at $398,400, so a typical sale lands on the higher schedule. Several deeds owe nothing at all: a parent-to-child deed, a transfer from an executor to an heir, and a deed recorded no later than 90 days after a divorce decree. Qualifying seniors and blind or disabled sellers pay a reduced partial rate. Your closing attorney or title company works out which column fits your sale.

Ocean County at a glance

Toms River is the county seat, and 33 municipalities make up the county. Mid-2025 population is estimated at 673,746, and Lakewood Township has the most people of any town. Owners live in 80.7 percent of the 243,843 households counted for 2020 to 2024. Typical household income is $89,863 and typical gross rent is $1,755.

With four of every five households owning, the typical seller is leaving a home lived in for years. The town where the house sits decides which tax collector you phone and which school district serves it, yet one county clerk records the deed for all 33 towns.

The Garden State Parkway has fed commuter growth since 1954, and NJ Transit buses connect Lakewood and Toms River with New York and Newark. If the house is near a bus stop, say so in the listing, since buyers ask about commutes. Many sellers here are settling a long-held home, and for them a smooth recording is usually the last item on a long list.

What should a seller ask the clerk before closing?

Find out what is already on record against the property. Liens appear in the land records, and a tax sale certificate recorded there must be paid off at closing. The certificate holder must file it in the clerk's deed room no later than 90 days after the sale, which is how an unpaid-tax lien can surface.

  • Order a property search for open mortgages, judgments and certificates under your name and the names of earlier owners.
  • Confirm which office takes your deed, the Toms River courthouse or a branch, and check that day's hours.
  • If the house came through an estate, ask your attorney which exemption belongs on the deed.
  • Ask whether an earlier deed went to the wrong county, since that can require a refund filing.

After filing, request a recorded copy so you hold proof that the transfer happened.

From signed contract to recorded deed

Once both sides sign, the title company or attorney searches the land records and prepares the deed with the full price stated. You sign, the transfer fee forms are clipped on, and the packet goes to the clerk of the land's home county. When the clerk accepts it, the record changes and the fee is collected.

Selling to a cash buyer as-is leaves this sequence alone. Recording still happens in the same county, on the same forms, with the same fee deducted from your side of the settlement sheet. What disappears is the repair list and the lender's timeline, which often makes recording the last open item before funds move.

Two habits keep this stage smooth. Read the deed draft line by line before signing, paying special attention to the stated price and the names, since those drive both the fee and the land record. And hold on to every receipt and the recorded copy afterward. If a question about the sale comes up years later, the clerk's record is the proof that the deed was filed, when it was filed, and in which county.

Frequently asked questions

Which office records a deed in Ocean County?

The Ocean County Clerk records deeds and other papers that affect ownership. Its courthouse office at 118 Washington Street in Toms River can be reached at (732) 929-2018.

Who pays the realty transfer fee on an Ocean County sale?

The seller. It is a charge on the seller for recording the deed.

Can I record my deed in a different county by mistake and fix it?

Yes. Record it again in the county where the land lies, file Form RTF-3 to get the State's share refunded, and ask the wrong county's recording office to return the county share.

Does an estate sale owe the transfer fee?

Not when an executor or administrator deeds the house to an heir or devisee named under the will or intestacy laws. If the executor sells to anyone else, the deed is not exempt.

How many Ocean County homes are owner-occupied?

About 80.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, across 243,843 households. An owned home sits at $398,400 at the middle of the range.

What the Hunterdon County Clerk does when a house sells

Every Hunterdon County deed and mortgage passes through the County Clerk, an elected office that calls itself the Keeper of the Records. Staff in the recording division examine each document for form, dates, signatures, acknowledgment and the property's location. Fees and transfer taxes are settled at the counter when the paper is filed. After that the clerk stamps a recording date, enters the document in the permanent index, sends an abstract of the deed to the local assessor, and hands the original back to the owner.

The office is at 71 Main Street in Flemington, and the mailing address is PO Box 2900, Flemington, NJ 08822. Counter service runs on weekdays until half past four, and the main line is (908) 788-1221. The clerk accepts e-filing, which lets whoever handles your closing submit the deed electronically, and posts a deed fraud warning worth reading before you sign anything.

Realty transfer fee

State law sets the transfer fee, and the clerk takes it at the counter in addition to ordinary recording charges. Each slice of the price carries its own rate, quoted for every $500 or part of $500. The rates below apply when the total price is over $350,000.

Realty transfer fee per $500 of consideration, sales above $350,000
Slice of the sale priceCharge per $500
First $150,000$2.90
$150,000 to $200,000$4.25
$200,000 to $550,000$4.80
$550,000 to $850,000$5.30
$850,000 to $1,000,000$5.80
Every dollar over $1,000,000$6.05

A sale at $350,000 or less uses lower rates. A residential sale priced over $1,000,000 adds a separate seller charge, the graduated percent fee, equal to 1 percent of the whole price and rising in steps to 3.5 percent past $3,500,000. Call the clerk to confirm which fee schedule applies to a deed over $1,000,000. For an exact number, run the price through the transfer fee calculator the clerk links.

Deeds exempt from the transfer fee

The state form carries a longer exemption list. These entries matter most to families and estates:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • An executor or administrator conveying to a devisee or heir to distribute the estate under a will or intestate succession.
  • Husband and wife, civil union partners, or parent and child.
  • A deed recorded inside 90 days of a divorce decree dissolving the marriage.
  • Paper that only gives or releases security for a debt, or fixes an earlier recorded deed.
  • A conveyance made on a sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.

An exemption has to be explained in detail on the affidavit. A simple exemption symbol is not enough.

The clerk will not record a deed unless it recites the consideration or carries an affidavit that states it. Consideration includes the money paid, the value of anything else given, and the balance of any mortgage the buyer assumes. Falsifying it is a fourth-degree crime under the state form's warning.

Hunterdon County property tax rates

Because the clerk forwards each deed to the municipal assessor, recording feeds directly into the tax roll. Hunterdon has 26 municipalities, and the state's 2025 table shows effective tax rates running from 1.782 in East Amwell to 3.483 in Hampton. Flemington, the county seat, is at a general rate of 2.736 and an effective rate of 2.984. Lambertville is at 1.902 effective, Clinton Town at 2.808 and High Bridge at 3.152.

The effective rate puts every town on the same footing, so a low general rate does not by itself mean a low bill. Bethlehem Township shows a general rate of 2.021 and an effective rate of 2.350, while Milford shows 4.027 general and 2.944 effective. Look up your own municipality before you choose a list price.

Hunterdon County housing snapshot

The 2025 estimate is 131,781 residents and 50,860 households. Owners occupy 85.1 percent of the homes, those homes are valued at a median $517,200, and a typical household earns $141,715. Gross rent in the middle of the range is $1,687. With so many owners, most sales are a family selling the home they live in, often a house with a well, a septic system or a long driveway that buyers will ask about.

Hunterdon has about 1,412 miles of public roads, and most of them, roughly 1,059 miles, are kept up by the municipalities. The county maintains about 238 miles and the state about 115, so the road at your driveway may belong to the town, the county or the state. Know which before you answer a buyer's question about plowing and repairs.

Searching Hunterdon County land records

The clerk's records go back to 1785, and the Record Room is open to the public on weekdays. Help from the Search Room staff is available by appointment at (908) 788-1380. Older records are being redacted to protect identities, with an online system planned after that work ends.

Sellers use these records to confirm the vesting deed, find an open mortgage that needs a release, or locate a recorded lien before a closing. The clerk's recording page also links a homeowner's guide to good deeds, a document reference manual and mortgage foreclosure help for owners behind on payments.

Hunterdon County does not take part in the Homeless Trust Fund, so budget no charge for it when you add up recording costs.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Hunterdon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to confirm with the clerk before closing

  • The current recording fee schedule, since only the transfer fee rates are reproduced here.
  • Whether the deed needs the seller's Affidavit of Consideration, required above $1,000,000 or when an exemption is claimed.
  • Who signs the affidavit: the form allows a grantor, a legal representative, or a title or lending officer.
  • How to deliver the package: at the counter, by mail or electronically.
  • The block and lot number, which the form requires and the municipal assessor can supply.
  • Whether the title company or attorney already holds the vesting deed, so the new deed's description matches it.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed, the affidavit and the transfer fee still go through the clerk in the same way, so the same checklist applies.

In practice the order runs like this: the closing attorney or title company prepares the deed, you sign it with any affidavit, the package goes to the counter or in electronically with the fees, and the clerk stamps the recording date. Once recorded, the clerk sends the deed abstract to the assessor and returns the original to the new owner. Ask your closing contact who is delivering the package and on what day, so nothing sits waiting while the fee clock and your payoff both keep running.

Frequently asked questions

Where does a Hunterdon County deed get recorded?

In the County Clerk's recording section on Main Street in Flemington. Call (908) 788-1221 before you go, since the office keeps weekday hours only.

Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Hunterdon County sale?

Sellers do. The recorder's block on the state form is labeled as paid by the seller, and the fee arrives at the counter with the deed.

Is a deed from an estate to an heir exempt from the transfer fee?

Yes, when the executor or administrator is carrying out a will or the intestacy laws. That case is listed among the form's exemptions.

Which Hunterdon County town has the highest effective tax rate?

Hampton leads the state's 2025 table at 3.483, while East Amwell sits at the bottom with 1.782.

Can I look up old Hunterdon County deeds?

Yes. Recorded instruments run from 1785 forward, and the public can visit the Record Room and the Search Room on weekdays.

Where to record a deed in Warren County

Deeds are recorded at the Warren County Clerk's Office, inside the Warren County Courthouse at 413 Second Street in Belvidere. The office takes every document that affects ownership or transfer of residential, commercial and industrial property in the county, in person, by mail or electronically.

  • Main office: 908-475-6211.
  • Records room: 908-475-6011.
  • Public records inquiries: 908-475-6220.
  • Fax: 908-475-6208.

Hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, and the clerk asks visitors to call ahead and book an appointment so staff can serve each person efficiently. If your closing is set for late afternoon, have the title company confirm the recording method in advance.

Staff can answer questions about what the office will accept, but they cannot give legal advice about a transfer, so questions about ownership go to your attorney. Recorded documents become public records. Anyone may copy or research them during normal business hours, which is how buyers, lenders and title searchers confirm who owns a parcel and what liens or mortgages are attached. A certified copy costs $5 and ordinary copies are $2 a page, with a print from the clerk's website at five cents a page.

Warren County housing market

Warren County sits in northwestern New Jersey along the Delaware River, across from Easton, Pennsylvania. Belvidere is the county seat and Phillipsburg, with 15,249 residents in 2020, is the largest of its 22 municipalities. The 2025 estimate for the county is 112,953 residents. Hackettstown has the county's only NJ Transit rail stop.

  • Homes occupied by owners: 75.1%.
  • Typical value of an owned home: $346,500.
  • Median household income: $100,869.
  • Median gross rent: $1,409.
  • Households: 45,391.

A typical home value of $346,500 sits just under the $350,000 line the state uses to set its Realty Transfer Fee rates, so many local sales fall close to that dividing line.

Recording fees

A deed costs $40 for the first page and $10 for each additional page, plus a $10 tax abstract that applies to some documents such as deeds, court orders and easements. Selected charges from the clerk's State of New Jersey fee schedule:

Selected Warren County Clerk recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
Deed, first page$40
Deed, each additional page$10
Mortgage, first page$30
Mortgage assignment, discharge, release or postponement, first page$40
Cancellation of mortgage$20
Data recording page, paper documents$10 (or $20 if missing)
Each name after the first five$6
Inheritance tax waiver$15
Certified copy$5
Copy of any document$2 per page

The county charges nothing toward the homeless fund, and a veteran's DD-214 filing is free. A deed that runs past one page adds $10 for each extra sheet, so ask your title company to count pages before you budget the recording cost.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Warren County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The Data Recording Page

This form lets the clerk index the land record. Paper recordings without it carry a $20 indexing charge instead of the $10 fee. All land recordings filed on paper, and electronically recorded deeds, must include it. For documents sent through e-file, the page is required for deeds only.

Your title company or attorney normally prepares it with the deed. If you are handling a family transfer yourself, download the form from the clerk's website and attach it to the first sheet. A missing page is an avoidable surcharge and a possible delay.

The state realty transfer fee

The New Jersey Realty Transfer Fee is collected on top of the clerk's recording charges. The state sets it by the consideration stated in the deed. Ask your closing attorney for the exact figure, especially if you may qualify for the senior citizen partial exemption.

  • An Affidavit of Consideration (RTF-1) must be filed with any deed that claims a full or partial exemption.
  • The state lists 16 reasons for a full exemption, and partial exemptions exist for seniors, blind or disabled owners, low and moderate income housing and new construction.
  • A deed recorded in the wrong county must be re-recorded in the county where the land sits, with a refund application to the State on Form RTF-3.

Send the deed to Belvidere only when the land lies in Warren County. If you are unsure which exemption fits, ask the attorney before the closing, because the affidavit travels with the deed and a mistake can mean a refund application later.

How to search Warren County land records

Use the clerk's online public land records search. Choose the guest option and run a search by name to see every recorded document linked to that person, or narrow it to a specific instrument. Major subdivision maps are searchable by municipality, and a full-size map print costs $9 a sheet.

The Computer Access service in the clerk's vault lets visitors look up mortgages, deeds, liens, trade names, inheritance tax waivers, building contracts and maps on terminals. Law firms and title agents that record often can open a charge account with the clerk for recording, certified copies and map copies. Those charge accounts are separate from the accounts set up with the website vendor, which exist only to print copies from the site.

The website search makes it easy to check your own recorded deed and any mortgage still open against the property before you list. If a satisfied mortgage does not show as discharged, raise it with your title company early, since a discharge costs $40 for the first page to record. The clerk's office also handles notary oaths, trade names and certificates for documents going out of state, so a seller who needs a clerk's certificate can arrange it at the same visit, at $5 per certificate.

What to bring when you sell

Most sellers never visit the clerk, because the attorney or title company files the deed. If you do record on your own, bring the signed and acknowledged deed with the tax block and lot, the Data Recording Page, the Affidavit of Consideration if an exemption applies, and payment for the first-page and additional-page charges. Call 908-475-6211 first to book the appointment the clerk asks for.

Plan the timing around the 4:30 pm close of the office, and remember that an e-filed deed skips the trip to Belvidere altogether. After recording, a certified copy gives you proof of what was filed, and the public records search lets you confirm the deed now appears under the buyer's name. A cash buyer purchasing as is uses the same office and the same fees, so a fast closing does not change the recording steps.

Frequently asked questions

What is the address of the Warren County Clerk's Office?

413 Second Street, Belvidere, NJ 07823, in the Warren County Courthouse. The main number is 908-475-6211, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Call ahead for an appointment.

What will a Warren County deed filing set me back?

The deed charge is $40 for the first page and $10 for each added page, with a $10 tax abstract on some documents. Add the state Realty Transfer Fee, which depends on the stated consideration.

Can a deed be recorded electronically in Warren County?

Yes. The clerk records documents in person, by mail or electronically. For e-filed documents the Data Recording Page is required for deeds only.

What happens if I leave out the Data Recording Page?

Paper documents without it are charged $20 for indexing, against $10 when the page is attached. Electronically recorded deeds also need the page or the same charge applies.

Is there a fee for filing a veteran's discharge in Warren County?

No. The fee schedule lists the DD-214 filing as no charge, along with a veteran's ID card and a peddler's license.
